title: pocket-conclave-context-probes-mateo-ruiz-2028-06-21
summary: Raw notes from a small reading circle ("Pocket Conclave") — quick reactions to three papers about contextual anchors, lightweight probes for KV caches, and episodic eviction heuristics. Mixing immediate takeaways + quick experiment seeds and rough cost/latency back-of-envelope ideas.
notes:
Purpose: stash half-formed thoughts before I forget them. Not polished.

Papers skimmed (fast):
- "Contextual Anchors: Stable Retrieval Signals for Long-Range Conditioning" (arXiv) — idea: insert short dense anchor vectors in the prefix to help model re-locate grounding tokens across very long sequences.
  - Takeaway: anchors act as cheap pointers, robustness comes from anchor spacing and embedding anisotropy.
  - Q: how do anchors interact with kv-cache sharding? If anchors are global, they could reduce cross-shard attention misses.

- "Probe Scaffolds for Lightweight Eval of KV Eviction" — proposes micro-probes that emulate eviction stress by synthetic key collisions and measures perplexity delta.
  - Takeaway: probes are cheap; useful as regression test for quantized models.
  - Idea: incorporate into our Optimize pipeline as pre-deploy quick checks.

- "Episodic Eviction Heuristics at Scale" (workshop short) — heuristic families (LRU variants, recency+topic, TTL by semantic shift). Shows that tiny TTL coding reduces hallucination spikes in long sessions.
  - Takeaway: TTL+topic boundaries promising for chat-oriented workloads.

Conference vibes / misc talks:
- Demo showed a toy where anchor tokens improved code generation consistency over 16k->64k jumps. Worth replicating on a small Redwood sandbox.
- Panel on "cheap evals" emphasized reproducible microbenchmarks (ship with seed corpora + deterministic prompt wrappers). This matches our move to lightweight eval harnesses.

Quick experiment seeds (ordered):
1) Anchor placement ablation: fixed spacing vs token-boundary-aware spacing. Metric: next-token perplexity on held-out doc, and ratio of top-1 stable token matches across window.
2) KV-shard-aware anchors: place anchors specific to shard boundaries and measure cross-shard attention counts. Metric: percent of attention mass that crosses shards and latency impact.
3) Probe-in-optimize: add scaffold probes to Optimize lint step. Probes: synthetic key collisions, TTL sweeps, quantized-model mismatch check.
4) TTL topic boundary detector: simple classifier over last 512 tokens to decide TTL expiry; compare against fixed TTL baseline.

Practical notes for running:
- Use small 7B model with fp16 on a dev instance to iterate fast. Enable kv-cache logging (debug) for 5–10 sessions; sample at 1s intervals for attention mass.
- Save probes as JSONL with fields: session_id, probe_type, seed_prompt, model_version, quant_config. Put files in GH repo under /probes/ for versioning.

Unresolved questions / flags:
- Anchors + quantization: do anchors survive 4-bit quantization well? If anchors rely on high precision for pointer-like behavior maybe degrade. Need microbench.
- How to avoid anchors becoming "memorized shortcuts" that cause overfitting in RLHF/online learning loops? May need regularization or slow update schedule.
- Operational cost: anchors add tokens — will increase token-billing and latency. Need rough per-session multiplier.

Rough estimates (back of napkin):
- Anchor overhead: 4 anchors x 3 tokens each = 12 tokens/session. If average session 500 tokens, token cost +2.4%. But overhead for KV writes may be disproportionate if anchors kept in cache long.
- Latency: adding anchors mostly affects prefix encoding once and KV insert cost; marginal per-token latency increase negligible in continuous generation but increases first-token latency by ~5–8ms on 8xA100 dev. Need measurement.

Immediate action items (for next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Prototype anchor ablation on 7B fp16; script: experiment/anchor_ablate.py (no infra changes).
- [ ] Add two scaffold probes to Optimize lint harness and run nightly on staging models.
- [ ] Draft a short doc for Solutions Engineering summarizing risk/cost/benefit for anchor experiments. Tag: @Leah Park to help with customer use-cases.

Links I want to keep:
- anchor paper arXiv (see linked_artifacts)
- lightweight-probes GH issue (linked above)

Notes-to-self: keep these experiments cheap and reproducible. Try to get deterministic seeds so probed deltas are <= 5% variance between runs. If variance >10% probably noise dominates.

Random heuristics I jotted:
- Anchor embedding noise annealing: when inserting anchors, add small gaussian noise during training/fine-tune so model doesn't latch onto exact vector.
- Probe TTL schedule: exponentially increasing TTL for long sessions (e.g., 1,2,4,8 minutes) to test sensitivity to eviction cadence.

Slack / tickets to create after prototype:
- GH: redwood-inference/probe-harness PR adding anchor probe config.
- Linear: OPT-anchors-01 (spec + rollout plan + rollback criteria).
- Slack mention: #optimize-experiments with two example traces.

End of dump. Will tidy into a PRD if any of the seeds look promising after first pass.
